1 April 2003

## Circular to Intermediaries licensed or registered for Dealing in Securities or Securities Margin Financing

## Obtaining Clients' Standing Authority under the Securities and Futures (Client Securities) Rules

The  Securities  and  Futures  Ordinance  (the  'SFO')  came  into  effect  today  and  the relevant existing legislation, such as the Securities Ordinance, was repealed.

Under the new regime, all legal requirements governing dealings with client securities and securities collateral are set out in the Securities and Futures (Client Securities) Rules (the 'Rules').

We would like to draw your attention to the following relevant changes in the Rules as compared to section 81, 81A and 121AB of the existing Securities Ordinance:

- (a) the standing authority must specify the validity period (limited to 12 months unless  the  client  in  question  is  a  professional  investor)  and  the  manner  in which it may be revoked (please refer to section 4(1) and (2));
- (b) 'deemed'  renewal  of  standing  authority  is  now  accepted  (please  refer  to section 4(3)); and
- (c) the scope of the authority has been slightly modified for securities dealers.

The  Rules, gazetted on 6 December  2002,  are  available at  the  Government Publications Centre, and accessible on the website of the Government Printer or via the SFC's website under the SFO section.

Should you have any questions, please contact Miss Lorraine Chan at 2842-7751.
